question:
A 54-year-old woman presents to the physician with discomfort in her upper left abdomen over the past month. Moreover, she has recently been feeling a bit tired. She has no history of any significant illness and takes no medications. Her vital signs are within normal limits. On percussion, the spleen size is 15 cm (5.9 in). Otherwise, the physical examination shows no abnormalities. The laboratory test results are as follows:
Hemoglobin 10 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 88 μm3
Leukocyte count 65,000/mm3
Platelet count 500,000/mm3
Two images of the peripheral blood smear are shown. Laboratory studies are most likely to show which of the following?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Hemoglobin 10 g/dL" -> "Low hemoglobin levels" -> "Possible anemia" -> 70% CHAIN: "Leukocyte count 65,000/mm3" -> "Elevated leukocyte count" -> "Possible leukocytosis" -> 80% CHAIN: "Platelet count 500,000/mm3" -> "Normal platelet count" -> "Excludes thrombocytopenia" -> 90% CHAIN: "Mean corpuscular volume 88 μm3" -> "Normal MCV" -> "Excludes macrocytic anemia" -> 90% CHAIN: "Spleen size 15 cm" -> "Splenomegaly" -> "Possible underlying hematologic disorder" -> 80% CHAIN: "Peripheral blood smear images" -> "May show abnormal cell morphology" -> "Further evaluation needed" -> 70%
analysis: The patient's presentation with splenomegaly, anemia, leukocytosis, and thrombocytosis is suggestive of chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). The laboratory findings, particularly the leukocyte count of 65,000/mm3 and platelet count of 500,000/mm3, are indicative of CML. The Philadelphia chromosome, a translocation between chromosomes 9 and 22 [t(9;22)], resulting in the BCR-ABL fusion gene, is characteristic of CML.
